citation_scope.promotion_rule: Only six path-changing, instrument, or falsifier works are promoted; all other seen IDs remain in the citation ledger.

records.title: Retrieval Meets Reasoning: Even High-school Textbook Knowledge Benefits Multimodal Reasoning

project_use_contract.reason: Borrow no/retrieval, text-versus-multimodal evidence, and k-budget arms; ScienceQA/VQA values are not portable to speech/omni.

paper_reported_experiment.setting: ScienceQA builds a 12k-plus question-reasoning-answer library and retrieves top-k multimodal exemplars; cross-dataset evaluation also covers A-OKVQA, MMBench and SEED.
reported_outcomes: On ScienceQA, paper Table 1 reports Gemini 58.08 to 91.75 with RMR.
The k ablation peaks at k=3 in the reported Gemini stratum.
Text-only retrieval is also strong, so the paper does not establish non-text necessity.

records.strongest_boundary_or_falsifier: Retrieved answer-bearing exemplars, text-only strength, and dataset-specific library construction leave answer leakage and modality-necessity alternatives unresolved.

records.title: M2A: Multimodal Memory Agent with Dual-Layer Hybrid Memory for Long-Term Personalized Interactions

project_use_contract.reason: Borrow raw-versus-semantic store, text/image retrieval, iterative refinement and modality ablations; enhanced LoCoMo is not the project's speech task.

paper_reported_experiment.setting: Enhanced LoCoMo with 10 long conversations, roughly 621 turns and 10k tokens per conversation and 214 images; GPT-4o-mini, Qwen3-VL-8B and GLM-4.6V-Flash; Qwen3-VL-32B and GPT-4o judge binary correctness.
reported_outcomes: Paper Table 1 reports Qwen full M2A 54.69 versus 41.38 without dual layer, 38.67 without iterative refinement and 50.59 without tri-path retrieval.
Visual-centric GPT-4o-mini stratum reports 43.27 for M2A and 30.69 for RAG.

records.strongest_boundary_or_falsifier: The full system changes storage, retrieval, iteration and modality together; automatic judges and the derived dataset limit clean attribution and cross-paper numeric comparison.

records.title: XSkill: Continual Learning from Experience and Skills in Multimodal Agents
records.authors: Guanyu Jiang, Zhaochen Su, Xiaoye Qu, Yi R. Fung

discovery.reason: D2 multimodal-skill with D3 persistence path

project_use_contract.reason: Borrow experience-versus-skill factorial arms, transfer across agent backbones and Average@4/Pass@4; visual-tool tasks are not target speech reproduction.

paper_reported_experiment.setting: VisualToolBench, TIR-Bench, MMSearch-Plus, MMBrowseComp and AgentVista; 100 sampled training tasks per benchmark; Gemini-2.5-Pro and Gemini-3-Flash with transfer to GPT-5-mini/o4-mini; four rollouts, top-k 3, maximum 20 turns.
reported_outcomes: VisualToolBench full reports 30.49 Average@4 and 46.73 Pass@4; without experience 27.45/42.52; without skill 26.64/41.12.

records.strongest_boundary_or_falsifier: Ground-truth answers are used during training-split accumulation and critique; frozen core therefore does not mean absence of supervised external learning.

records.title: GEMS: Agent-Native Multimodal Generation with Memory and Skills

discovery.reason: D0 system bundle with D2/D3 components

project_use_contract.reason: Use as a bundle-level system/component boundary; sequential integration cannot support separate memory or skill causal claims.

paper_reported_experiment.setting: Multimodal generation benchmarks include GenEval, GenEval2, DPG-Bench, OneIG and WISE; the principal ablation is a sequential build-up of agent, memory and skills.
reported_outcomes: The paper reports improvements for the complete GEMS bundle and averages selected GenEval2/Z-Image-Turbo ablations over three runs.
source_locators: PDF pp.5-7, main results and ablation

records.strongest_boundary_or_falsifier: Sequential, non-factorial integration changes the system harness while adding memory and skills; individual capability attribution is not identified.

records.title: Skill Retrieval Augmentation for Agentic AI

discovery.reason: D2 skill retrieval/incorporation instrument and falsifier

project_use_contract.reason: Borrow oracle-skill, retrieval, loading and hard-negative decomposition to measure selection utility separately from task success.

paper_reported_experiment.setting: SRA-Bench has 5,400 instances, 636 manually constructed gold skills and 26,262 skills across six reasoning/coding benchmarks and six open models.
reported_outcomes: The paper reports that full injection is brittle and progressive disclosure is more stable under hard negatives.
Models often load a skill regardless of whether a gold skill is available or needed, separating retrieval from incorporation.
source_locators: PDF pp.10-12, hard-negative and loading analyses

records.strongest_boundary_or_falsifier: High retrieval recall or skill loading does not imply correct incorporation or downstream utility; this directly blocks retrieval-quality-to-capability inference.

records.title: MMSkills: Towards Multimodal Skills for General Visual Agents

discovery.reason: D2 causally testable multimodal-skill direct path

project_use_contract.reason: Borrow no-skill/text-only/state-card/image and direct-versus-branch-loading arms; rebuild for speech state and acoustic milestones.

paper_reported_experiment.setting: OSWorld, macOSWorld, VAB-Minecraft and Super Mario Bros; six large and small VLM backbones; skills combine procedures, state cards and multi-view keyframes.
reported_outcomes: On OSWorld, the paper reports full versus no-skill gains across all six listed backbones.
Text-only can regress: Gemini 3.1 Pro reports 40.76 with text-only versus 44.08 without skills, while full MMSkills reports 50.11.

records.strongest_boundary_or_falsifier: Text-only regression and model/domain heterogeneity show that procedural content alone can interfere; MM3 necessity requires exact same-run image/state ablations and is not granted here.

records.title: Anything2Skill: Compiling External Knowledge into Reusable Skills for Agents

project_use_contract.reason: Borrow paired Base/RAG/Skill/Skill+RAG design to test whether compilation adds value beyond access to the same source knowledge.

paper_reported_experiment.setting: qsv and GitHub-CLI command-line benchmarks; GitHub corpus has 110 documents and 179 compiled skills; all four arms use gpt-5.4-mini.
reported_outcomes: qsv task success: 81.60, 95.41, 91.95 and 98.85 for the four arms.
GitHub-CLI task success: 64.70, 76.50, 82.30 and 94.10.

records.strongest_boundary_or_falsifier: Custom text-only benchmarks and absent uncertainty in the main table prevent treating the setting as multimodal or as a target reproduction anchor.

records.title: RESOURCE2SKILL: Distilling Executable Agent Skills from Human-Created Multimodal Resources

discovery.reason: D2 multimodal-resource skill construction direct path

project_use_contract.reason: Borrow matched task briefs, same-backend with/without skills, representation/source/selection ablations, blinded artifact judging and human calibration.

paper_reported_experiment.setting: Seven authoring domains with 80 matched briefs per domain in the main study and 40 per ablation; four model backends; artifact rendering and blinded automatic judging with human calibration.
reported_outcomes: The paper reports an average main improvement of 11.9 percentage points and positive aggregate change in 26 of 28 model-domain cells.
Selection ablation reports 68.9 for the proposed method versus 60.0 embedding, 64.2 BM25+embedding, 58.0 random and 57.3 no skill.
Human A/B reports 68.0% skill preference, 20.5% ties and 11.5% no-skill preference.
source_locators: PDF pp.30-31, judge and human calibration

records.strongest_boundary_or_falsifier: No matched-token raw-resource RAG arm isolates skill compilation from source access; automatic judges and programmatic-tool domains constrain generalization.

records.title: AutoSkill: Experience-Driven Lifelong Learning via Skill Self-Evolution

project_use_contract.reason: Reference the explicit extraction/revision/retrieval lifecycle and skill-versus-memory distinction; no paired task-performance result supports borrowing an effect size.

paper_reported_experiment.setting: WildChat-1M conversations longer than eight turns are split by Chinese/English and GPT-3.5/GPT-4; the paper reports SkillBank counts, tags and qualitative cases.
reported_outcomes: Four subsets contain 1,145 to 10,243 conversations and 224 to 631 extracted skills.
No matched with/without-skill task-performance experiment is reported.

records.strongest_boundary_or_falsifier: Version increments and corpus counts demonstrate operation, not improvement, transfer, correct maintenance or resistance to accumulated error.

records.title: SKILLFOUNDRY: Building Self-Evolving Agent Skill Libraries from Heterogeneous Scientific Resources
records.authors: Paper author list on official arXiv record

discovery.reason: Heterogeneous-resource skill construction and validation component

project_use_contract.reason: Reference resource-to-skill validation and domain workflow transfer; the scientific task and tool stack are too distant for target reproduction.

paper_reported_experiment.setting: Same coding agent with and without skills on six MoSciBench datasets, plus cell-type annotation and a three-replicate expert-scored scDRS workflow transfer.
reported_outcomes: MoSciBench mean Repo-Acc rises from 61.19 to 66.73 and Paper-Acc from 43.85 to 53.05; execution remains 100%.
Cell-type annotation reports coverage/accuracy 81.1/68.5 without skill and 99.2/82.9 with skill.
scDRS mean RMSE falls from 0.11 to 0.02 across three reported replicates.

records.strongest_boundary_or_falsifier: Most mined skills are internally tested, downstream coverage is narrow, and task-specific skill construction can change the workflow rather than isolate representation alone.

records.title: SkillFlow: Benchmarking Lifelong Skill Discovery and Evolution for Autonomous Agents
records.authors: Paper author list on official arXiv record

discovery.reason: Strong negative and lifecycle benchmark for self-evolving skills

project_use_contract.reason: Borrow sequential family-local evaluation, empty-library baseline, raw-history control, cost and library-health measures, and negative-transfer audit.

paper_reported_experiment.setting: 166 runnable tasks in 20 task families; empty initial library; 11 model variants across Claude Code, Codex CLI, Qwen-Coder and Kimi-CLI; tasks update family-local skills sequentially.
reported_outcomes: Effects range from +8.43 completion points for Claude Opus 4.6 to -6.02 for GPT-5.3 Codex in the reported aggregate.
MiniMax M2.7 and Qwen settings can regress while increasing turns, cost or skill count.
Raw-history control on Opus 4.6 reaches 51.04, below vanilla and the full protocol.

records.strongest_boundary_or_falsifier: Incorrect skills propagate error, skill inflation can reduce performance, and library repair—not creation alone—appears to govern benefit.

records.title: SkillsBench: Benchmarking How Well Agent Skills Work Across Diverse Tasks

discovery.reason: Paired skill-efficacy instrument and failure analysis

project_use_contract.reason: Borrow fixed-task paired trials, deterministic verifiers, multiple harnesses, invocation-rate audit, compactness ablations and negative-task analysis.

paper_reported_experiment.setting: 87 tasks across eight domains, 18 model-harness configurations, four terminal harnesses, matched no-skill and curated-skill conditions, three public trials per configuration-task-condition cell in fresh pinned containers.
comparisons: self-generated skills on three dedicated harnesses
reported_outcomes: Mean pass rate is 33.9 without skills and 50.5 with curated skills, a reported +16.6 points.
Thirteen of 87 tasks have negative skill deltas.
Self-generated skills fall below no-skill on all three tested dedicated harnesses.
source_locators: PDF p.7, Table 3 and task failures
PDF p.8, design ablations and limitations

records.strongest_boundary_or_falsifier: Skill injection adds context; no matched-length random/irrelevant/source-document control fully isolates procedural structure, and harness choice materially changes the effect.

records.title: Evaluating Very Long-Term Conversational Memory of LLM Agents
records.authors: Adyasha Maharana, Dong-Ho Lee, Sergey Tulyakov, Mohit Bansal, Francesco Barbieri, Yuwei Fang

discovery.reason: Original LoCoMo dataset and memory measurement contract

project_use_contract.reason: Borrow temporal/multi-hop/adversarial memory outcomes, answer-turn provenance and retrieval-noise controls; do not call M2A's derived dataset the same revision.

paper_reported_experiment.setting: 50 human-verified long conversations averaging about 300 turns and 9k tokens over up to 35 sessions; QA, event summarization and multimodal dialogue generation tasks.
comparisons: multimodal generation with summary or retrieved observations
reported_outcomes: Human QA F1 is 87.9 while reported model baselines remain substantially lower.
Observation RAG can improve QA, but increasing retrieved observations lowers signal-to-noise and can hurt.
For QA and event summarization, images are replaced by captions; direct images are used only in multimodal dialogue generation.

records.strongest_boundary_or_falsifier: Caption substitution means most memory QA evidence is not a causal test of visual-memory necessity; the synthetic generation pipeline also limits ecological validity.

records.title: Memory-R1: Enhancing Large Language Model Agents to Manage and Utilize Memories via Reinforcement Learning
records.authors: Paper author list on official arXiv record

discovery.reason: RL-trained memory manager and answer-agent boundary

project_use_contract.reason: Reference the action space, downstream answer reward and reward-metric disagreement; parameter training and text-only data make it a boundary, not a reproduction anchor.

paper_reported_experiment.setting: LoCoMo with 152/81/1307 question train/validation/test split plus zero-shot MSC and LongMemEval; LLaMA-3.1-8B and Qwen-2.5 3B/7B/14B; PPO/GRPO-trained memory manager and answer agent.
reported_outcomes: On LLaMA-3.1-8B, overall Memory-R1-GRPO reports F1 45.02, BLEU-1 37.51 and judge 62.74.
The paper reports performance drops when removing the trained manager, trained answer agent or memory distillation.
Judge-based reward raises judge score but lowers F1/BLEU-1 relative to exact-match reward.

records.strongest_boundary_or_falsifier: Core policies are fine-tuned; reward choice changes output length and metric ranking, so it cannot be counted as training-free control or multimodal memory evidence.
